podcast.title: Cat Cloning
podcast.body: In 2006, Liam Lynch successfully had his cat cloned, a notable personal event. "In 2006, he successfully had his cat cloned."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Career
podcast.body: Before his music career, Liam Lynch held diverse jobs including dishwasher, Blockbuster clerk, telemarketer, and wax museum guide. He also worked in AI for Sony, attempting to teach tricks to the company's robot dog, AIBO. "He has had jobs as a dishwasher, a clerk at Blockbuster, a telemarketer, and a guide in a wax museum."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 50 Biggest Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of All Time: Part 2 (40-31)

podcast.title: Education and MTV Work
podcast.body: Liam Lynch studied music in Liverpool before getting a job writing, directing, scoring, and producing "The Sifl and Ollie Show," an MTV puppet program. "He then studied music and liver pool, and then got a job writing, directing, scoring, and producing an MTV puppet program called The Cifl and Ollie Show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 50 Biggest Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of All Time: Part 2 (40-31)

podcast.title: Film Director
podcast.body: Liam Lynch directed the 2006 movie for Tenacious D, as well as a documentary about the band. "Liam Lynch directed their 2006 movie, Plus a Tenacious D documentary."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 50 Biggest Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of All Time: Part 2 (40-31)

podcast.title: Music Video Director
podcast.body: After his hit song, Liam Lynch went on to direct music videos for prominent bands such as Foo Fighters, Queens of the Stone Age, Eagles of Death Metal, Royal Blood, No Doubt, Weird Al, They Might Be Giants, and Tenacious D. "He went on to direct music videos for the Foo's, Queen of the Stone Age, Eagles of Death Metal, Royal Blood, No Doubt, Weird L. They might be giants in Tenacious D."

podcast.title: Paranormal Activity Channel
podcast.body: Liam Lynch and his wife record paranormal activity and upload the footage to their YouTube channel, "The Spark Club." "He and his wife record paranormal activity, which he uploads to a YouTube channel called The Spark Club."
